analysis.title: DeskTalk - US equity check: Technically speaking
key_insights: US equities are under heavy pressure on Nov 19, 2026 with the SPX down 1.5% at 14:15 EST and on track for a sixth consecutive losing session, the longest streak since April 2024.
Nvidia's earnings were described as a blowout but did not work as the clearing event markets hoped for.
The Anthropic IPO, a second potential clearing event, debuted 34% above issue price and then reversed sharply, and sentiment worsened further.
The selloff is broad: all 11 sectors are down and over 80% of index constituents are weaker.
Spot VIX is at 28 after spending most of the month above 20.
Cash desk flows are skewed to buying Healthcare, Industrials and Energy, and to selling Info Tech, Financials, Consumer Discretionary, Comm Services and Consumer Staples.
SPX broke below a key support trend line from the Liberation Day low at $7,245 (ref $7,218).
Systematic flows are a key driver, with all indices 'max short' and sellers into strength. SPX (ESZ6) is roughly 3% from the $7,474 'reduce shorts' trigger and NDX is 6.5% away.
Citi's equity trading strategy desk expects the next leg of idiosyncratic catalysts after earnings season to be year-end investor days, with Q4 typically a big quarter for them.

earnings_insights: Nvidia's earnings were described as a 'blowout' but the stock and market did not rally, so they did not act as a clearing event. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
Earnings season is coming to a close. Citi's equity trading strategy desk expects year-end investor days to be the next leg of idiosyncratic catalysts.
risk_factors: A sixth consecutive losing session for SPX would be the longest streak since April 2024.
Failed 'clearing events' (Nvidia earnings, the Anthropic IPO) point to deteriorating sentiment.
SPX has broken below the support trend line from the Liberation Day low.
Systematic sellers are positioned max short and sell into strength, which adds to downside pressure until the reduce-shorts trigger is reached.
vol_and_positioning: Spot VIX is at 28, after spending most of this month above 20.
All indices are 'max short' in systematic positioning, with systematic flows selling into strength.
SPX (ESZ6) is roughly 3% away from the $7,474 trigger to 'reduce shorts', and NDX is 6.5% away. The note refers readers to the Citi Derivs CTA Update.
Breadth is poor: all 11 sectors are down and more than 80% of constituents are weaker.
